From time to time I like to remind people that I am not the best trader in the world. I'm not the greatest chartist or technician in the world. I'm not the richest. I'm not the smartest. I'm not a celebrity or have any desire to try to gain fame. I have plenty of flaws. I have made plenty of wrong calls and mistakes in the past and will continue to do so, I promise you that. I leave all my wrong tweets from the past up in its glory for those who ever want to go back and bask in my misery lol. 

This is not a pity party. Or an attempt to fish for compliments. But a realization. A truth. A humble post.

I started Fintwit because I just had a passion for the Stock Market and a deep passion for charting stocks. That is it. In its most simplest form. I just wanted to blog about it and share it on the internet. And I just kept doing it. How time flies.

I don't know when this journey of mine will end or if it ever will. But I really do wake up every day 24/7, 365, and enjoy doing this. Degen? Perhaps. Addiction? Certainly. But I always say, whatever floats your boat and makes you happy. Then go and get that happiness.

-Heis

tweets.text:
Reeeeally interesting reaction to my very simple onliner appreciation for @CypherPunksArt yesterday. In a place so drenched in apathy, disinterest and straight up death, that’s definately a good sign. Lots of angry and hating messages too, coupled with a couple of very excited ones from high signal account too, again a combo that does well. 

But mostly pissed off. So let me double down on a deeper dive and some random considerations and takeaways.

First things first, it’s clear that almost everyone here is oneshotted by AI and slop, and no one reads. The collection has a release method that is nouns style. That’s where anything Nouns similiarities ends. There is no dao.

The punk you get gives you access to a truly permissionless mint platform, where you can mint/publish whatever you like for basically no cost besides gas. Forever. The platform is forever permissionless. 

This is what got me here and excited in the first place: you know Blur died, like I always said it would? Magiceden pretty much did too. So many other platforms are on their way, with Niftygateway being a great example of a centralized permissioned platform telling you how and what you can do with your shit, and then taking it down with them when they died: millions in art lost forever, and beautiful imagery and artist’s works never accessible again.

Opensea is now basically a monopoly, with Gondi the only quality alternative, and that’s not a good spot to be given how they always treated their colustomers, their obvious diregard for users with the forver carrot of an airdrop, and their pivot away from NFT’s and towards perps swaps and whatever other overcrowded arena they’ll zero themselves out in.

thread_tweets.text:
2/ So yeah, a permissionless alternative sounds great and frankly necessary to me. For now it’s more manyfold than it is OS, clearly there is a lot of work to do, otherwise these would be going for several thousands of dollars, not the cost of a dinner out. 

The main risk is you’re super reliant on @kenny83, the lead, to keep delivering and not get too greedy on mint proceeds. He comes highly reccomended and all my interactions with him tell me he’s here to stay, but in this space you never know, and my disappointment list has been endless. 

Another interesting thing coming with the cyberphunks is Etched, a fully onchain art magazine that talks everything web3 and digital art every month. 

A high quality, onchain “fanzine” that is independent enough is something this place has lacked for a long time. 

There’s also a dedicated chatroom for holders, and everytime you win an auction you get to sign a message forever onchain and linked to the master book of the cypherpunks. A sort of time capsule for the collection that snapshots the mint day in context.

Finally, yeh they pfp well, and although clearly punks adjacent, they pay hommage more than being derivative. Traits like the xcopy eyes and doomer T, the moneyalotta money printer machine, the golden apes, the squiggles hat, and clearly the 9 alien punks like the og’s they pay tribute too: I set the record way overspending on the best one in the collection imho, if I ever change pfp that’s probably gonna be it.

The auction model clearly brings back that “gather around the fire” mint excitment we used to have around these parts, and more and more people just tune in for the show and curiosity. That’s collectors driven, something this space severely missed. It’s funny how for the first two mints the biggest names in this space where all there every day battling it out, but not a single word was out on socials about it: no competition wanted on those first 100 serials 😂 

Bullish. 

So yeah, make up your own mind, this entire space is in the shitters right now, but maybe do some actual research before opening your mouth. 

As for me, I have only three projects I truly still love in here besides digital art itself:

6529 chain launching in a few months is the one thing I’m looking forward to the most, not only in web3 but crypto at large. It’s a bastion of hope in so many ways, necessary at a core. I think people are severely underestimating the scope and importance of it all.

Then BAYC always, as the only IP truly standing the test of times, and with the Otherside resource game finally kickstarting that whole eco + Mudwater being underestimated in what it represents and what it can become. 

And now, cypherpunks as a new socially owned and directed way to mint and transact and access and talk about our own little space. 

That’s my dark horse.
